Figure 1: Three benchmark examples. (a) A localized defect weakens a lemma until it becomes false. (b) A compound state contains two linked defects on the target path and one disconnected node. (c) In a proof-authoring state, the graph is correct but the remaining theorem still needs proof content. Statements are abbreviated; Table 1 lists all failure families.

Figure 3: Cumulative solved states as the per-task budget increases, for both models. Panels (a) and (c) use completion tokens; panels (b) and (d) use provider price. All four use the same 142 initial states, count solved as in Table 5, and stop charging a task when it is first solved. The token axes are identical, so the two models’ left-hand panels can be read against each other; the price axes are not, because Qwen3.6-Flash output is priced an order of magnitude above DeepSeek-V4-Flash’s.
Figure 2: The repair loop used by all three interfaces. The harness applies one candidate action, Lean checks the resulting module, and the graph check returns structured feedback for the next step.
